rationale:
Evidence: all 80 development trials (iterations 0 to 3 in the feedback, plus iteration 4 in the scoreboard) ended off_track with no finishes. The best design so far is iteration 4 (score 91.4; oval progress 0.44, s-bend 0.15, slalom 0.07). Max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.064 on nearly every design, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Line loss occurs about 1 to 2 times per run. With five sensors at x = ±0.016 and 8 mm footprints, the outer sensor reaches only about ±0.020 m, so the tape stops being seen once the robot is roughly 0.032 m off-centre. That leaves about 0.03 m of recovery margin before the off-track limit, and the search mode (last_direction at throttle 0.35) cannot recover in that space. Steering oscillation is low (about 0.19 at most), so the correction is sluggish or under-ranged rather than jittery.

Change (one structural change, controller held at iteration 4 values): widen the sensor span to seven 8 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 (step 0.008), y = 0.03, with weights [-2, -1.3, -0.6, 0, 0.6, 1.3, 2]. Outer sensors now see the tape from about 0.036 m off-centre, so line loss should come later and the controller gets more warning. I placed them at y = 0.03, not 0.05, because iteration 2 changed the forward offset and span together and scored worse, so I want to isolate the span. Controller values match iteration 4 (kp 3.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.4, base_speed 1.3, last_direction), so any change in result comes from the sensing span.

Expected result: line_loss_events drop toward 0 to 1 per run, max_error falls below 0.06 on oval and s-bend, and progress rises above 0.44 on oval. Hypotheses: H1, the narrow sensor span causes the line loss at bends, so widening it extends the distance covered before loss. H2, the iteration 4 gains are adequate for the wider signal. Measurements needed next: line_loss_events and max_error per track (to see whether loss still happens and where), progress on s-bend and slalom, and steering_oscillation (to check that the wider signal does not add jitter). If the robot now holds the line but is too slow, raise base_speed; if max_error still reaches 0.06 with no line loss, raise kp before adding more kd.
